2026 Super AI SmartCraft Challenge is a global robotics competition open to the Elementary, Junior, and Senior  Groups. Each team consists of 1–2 students and 1 coach.
The competition can be used as part of STEM innovation practice and can be deeply integrated into classroom teaching and science popularization activities. It supports schools in delivering AI and robotics education, empowering teaching innovation and the development of hands-on practical skills.

SmartCraft Challenge Overview
This year’s robotics challenge, themed “SmartCraft · Grains,” traces the origins of ancient Chinese agricultural wisdom. In this competition, robots take on the role of intelligent craftsmen, precisely identifying grains and carefully sowing them. Through programs and code, contestants will bring to life the practical spirit and innovation of meticulous farming.
Participants are required to independently design and build a robot using controllers, drivers, sensors, and plastic building components. By combining programming and wireless remote control, teams drive their robots to complete assigned tasks through inter-team collaboration and interaction, followed by communication and presentation.
The SmartCraft field is divided into red and blue sides, with two participants on each side. The competition consists of two phases: Autonomous and Remote Control.
During the Autonomous Phase, participants complete tasks on their own side of the field to earn points. In the Remote-Control Phase, participants operate their robots via remote control to throw their own props onto the opposing team’s Farming Tower to score points. The team with the higher total score wins.

productInfo.title: 2.4G Wireless Transceiver (Building Block Version)
productInfo.content:
BE-9237 Wireless Transceiver (Building Block Version)

 


1. Introduction:

JMP-BE-9237 is a 2.4GHz wireless communication module that uses encrypted addressing for easy pairing. It allows data exchange with any device or module within range. The module automatically switches between transmit and receive modes, filtering out interference from other devices operating on the same frequency. Firmware upgrade support enables ongoing improvements and feature enhancements.

 

2. Description:

After the module is powered on, it uses the default communication password to communicate. If the module has never been paired with another module, the default communication password is 1234567; if the module has been paired before, the communication password will be the pairing code used during the last pairing.

During module pairing, the communication password is automatically negotiated by the two paired modules and saved even after a power-off. The next time the module is powered on, this pairing code will be used as the default communication password.

 

To avoid interference from other users, when programming in the RoboEXP software, be sure to call the corresponding programming module to change the password or use the pairing button on the module to pair before use. For wireless communication, the passwords on both ends must be exactly the same to establish a connection.

The password specified through the RoboEXP module is a temporary modification and will not be saved after power-off (only the pairing code set via the pairing button will be retained).

 

In special situations, the wireless module may experience packet loss due to prolonged interference on the same frequency or a weak signal. (Within a preset time range, the module will attempt to resend the data multiple times.) In such cases, the module will return relevant information to prompt the user for further action.

 

3. Precautions:

Please avoid using the module in environments with strong interference. For example, if there are multiple Bluetooth or Wi-Fi devices nearby, the wireless channels may overlap and affect the communication quality of the module.

In dry environments, the module may be damaged by strong static electricity from the human body or other objects. Please ensure proper electrostatic discharge (ESD) protection before use.

This module is intended only for general entertainment or student competitions. It is strictly prohibited to use it in industrial, aerospace, biomedical, or similar fields. For applications in other areas, please consult our company before use.

productInfo.title: Attitude Sensor V1.1
productInfo.content:
Attitude Sensor V1.1

 

1. Overview

       

The BE-2621 Attitude Sensor is a precision orientation reference system designed for robotics applications. It provides 3-axis acceleration and 3-axis gyroscope data, as well as direct Euler angle output for intuitive and easy use.

Typical applications include self-balancing vehicles, gimbals, remote controllers, multi-degree-of-freedom (DOF) robots, gesture recognition devices, drones, and submarines.

 

 


 

No.


 

Description

 

①

Label: BE-2621

BE: Indicates electronic components of the building block robot

26: Refers to attitude measurement type

21: Refers to I²C output for attitude data

②

Standard telephone port interface

③

Indicator light

④

3D coordinate axes

 

2. Features

Wide operating voltage range: 4.5 V – 5 V

Update rate: 400 Hz

Communication: I²C

Interface: ZMROBO RCU standard telephone port

 

3. Instructions for Use

The BE-2621 Attitude Sensor is used like other sensors:

Connect it to the controller, define the hardware type, then use the corresponding programming icon to read data.

 

l The module returns numeric values and can be connected to ports P1–P8.

 

l Ensure the module is installed in a horizontal position for accurate measurements.

 

l In programming, configure the module parameters as needed, then process the returned values for calculations or logic control.

 

l Example programs can be found in RoboEXP under:

File > Open Example > Other Modules > Attitude Measurement Module

 

4. Working Principle

The BE-2621 Attitude Measurement Module fuses data from its built-in 3-axis accelerometer and 3-axis gyroscope. After filtering, it integrates gyroscope angular velocity over time to calculate rotation angles, which are corrected using accelerometer data. This process yields the Roll, Pitch, and Yaw angles.

 

Due to the lack of a fixed reference in the horizontal plane, Yaw may drift over time, which is normal. The controller reads all data via the I²C interface.

 

 5. Usage Notes

 

1) After powering on, keep the AHRS sensor stationary and level for about 8 seconds until the indicator LED stops flashing. This allows the sensor to stabilize, especially the Yaw reading. (8 seconds is optional but recommended.)

 

2) Roll and Pitch angles are corrected using 3-axis accelerometer vectors, yielding relatively accurate results. Yaw, calculated by integrating the Z-axis gyroscope, lacks magnetometer correction and is prone to drift. Accuracy is acceptable within ±90°; repeated rotations may cause cumulative error.

 

3) Euler angles are subject to gimbal lock near ±90° Pitch, which may cause calculation singularities. It is advised to avoid such positions during use.

 

(4) Data Format & Conversion:

The returned values are 16-bit signed integers (int16). To get the actual readings:

 

Roll, Pitch, Yaw: divide the raw value by 10 to get degrees.

Example: 1508 → 150.8°

 

Acceleration (X/Y/Z): divide by 100 to get values in g.

Example: 103 → 1.03g

 

Angular velocity: divide by 10 to get values in °/s.

Example: 2506 → 250.6°/s

 

Convert to float as needed in your application.
